entities.name: Emanuel Maiberg
entities.explain: 调查记者，404 Media联合创始人，长期追踪科技行业内幕

entities.name: 404 Media
entities.explain: 一家独立科技调查媒体，由前Motherboard记者创立，专注数字权利与技术伦理报道

entities.name: France24
entities.explain: 法国国际新闻电视台，由政府资助，以多语种面向全球播报

entities.name: AI训练数据
entities.explain: 用来教人工智能模型学习和生成内容的海量文本、图片等素材

entities.name: AI woodchipper（AI碎木机）
entities.explain: 比喻说法，指将图书拆解销毁后高速扫描、化为AI训练数据的工业化流程

cards.summary: 调查记者Emanuel Maiberg在France24节目中披露，大量稀有图书正通过匿名市场被批量收购，运往大型扫描工厂。在那里，书籍装订被拆除，书页以极高速度被扫描处理，最终成为AI训练数据。整条供应链全球化且刻意不透明，Maiberg指出这种行为背后的动机并非恶意，而是冷漠——对书籍本身价值的漠视。
cards.relevant: AI训练数据的来源合法性正成为全球监管焦点。此调查揭示了图书被大规模销毁用于AI训练的隐秘产业链，涉及版权、文化遗产保护与科技伦理等多重议题，对正在制定AI监管政策的各国政府具有参考意义。
cards.context: 随着大语言模型竞争加剧，科技公司对高质量文本数据的需求激增。公开网络数据逐渐枯竭后，各公司转向图书等受版权保护的资源。此前已有报道指出部分AI公司扫描图书用于训练，但此次调查进一步揭示了从收购、拆解到扫描的完整工业化流程及其不透明性。
cards.source_analysis: France24是法国政府资助的国际公共电视台，在科技议题上倾向从欧洲视角审视美国科技巨头的影响力。受访者Maiberg所在的404 Media以独立深度调查著称，报道立场偏向批判科技公司权力扩张、维护数字权利。
cards.social_impact: 若涉及数百万册图书，意味着大量可能绝版的珍本从公共流通中永久消失，对学术研究和文化传承造成不可逆损失。事件也引发公众对AI公司数据获取方式合法性与道德性的质疑，可能推动各国加快AI训练数据透明化立法。

One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site. Issued on: François Picard is pleased to welcome investigative journalist Emanuel Maiberg, Co-founder of 404 Media. As we embark on AI's uncharted waters, Maiberg has made a most unexpected discovery:: the mass acquisition, dismemberment and scanning of rare books for use as training data. His investigation reveals a globalised and deliberately opaque supply chain in which books purchased through anonymous marketplaces can ultimately arrive at large-scale scanning facilities, where their bindings are removed so that pages can be processed at great speed. Yet Maiberg’s analysis reaches far beyond the striking dystopian image of books being destroyed. What happens when knowledge changes form, changing ownership and accessibility? A book can circulate between readers, libraries and generations. Once destroyed and absorbed into a proprietary AI system, however, its contents survive virtually, encoded within a model whose outputs and rules of access are controlled by a private company. The paradox is striking: an industry seeking to ingest ever more human knowledge may simultaneously will erase the very sources of that knowledge. Maiberg is careful not to portray this process as a diabolical campaign to rid society of books. His more unsettling interpretation is that the destruction is driven by something more mundane: indifference. In the race to build increasingly capable AI systems, books become inputs to be optimized, and their destruction becomes an acceptable operational cost. That logic, he argues, belongs to a broader concentration of informational power already visible in search engines and social media. And now AI is taking it to a whole new level. The investigation therefore raises a larger question in the world of culture and academia: as more of the world's accumulated knowledge is mediated through AI systems, who controls the infrastructure through which that knowledge can be accessed?

cards.summary: 距离美国中期选举不到两个月，网络上出现一系列AI伪造视频，内容为名人看似在谴责民主党。经France24核实，这些视频均为虚假内容，由人工智能生成，属于俄罗斯针对民主党的虚假信息行动的一部分。
cards.relevant: 中期选举结果将决定美国国会控制权，外国势力利用AI干预选举引发对选举公正性和AI监管的担忧。
cards.context: 美国中期选举临近，各方势力加大舆论争夺。近年来俄罗斯被多次指控通过社交媒体和虚假信息干预美国选举，此次首次大规模使用AI生成视频进行政治抹黑。
cards.source_analysis: France24是法国公共国际新闻频道，其'Truth or Fake'栏目专门进行事实核查，立场偏向揭露虚假信息，具有较高的可信度。
cards.social_impact: AI伪造内容降低了制造虚假政治信息的门槛，可能误导选民、加剧政治极化，对选举安全和社交媒体平台的内容审核构成新挑战。

cards.summary: 俄罗斯和中国在联合国安理会联合行使否决权，阻止了美国提出的一项延长联合国对伊朗核计划监督的决议。这一投票结果凸显了世界大国之间在美国对伊朗施压问题上的深刻分歧。
cards.relevant: 此次否决表明，尽管美国试图通过联合国框架维持对伊朗核活动的国际监督，但中俄两国明确反对这一路线，大国博弈可能使伊朗核问题进一步脱离多边管控框架。
cards.context: 美国此前一直推动联合国继续对伊朗核计划进行监督，作为其对伊施压策略的一部分。然而俄罗斯和中国认为这种做法不利于外交解决，选择在安理会投票中联手否决美方提案。
cards.source_analysis: 《纽约时报》是美国主流媒体，报道通常从美国视角出发，倾向于强调美国外交努力面临的阻力以及大国之间的对立。
cards.social_impact: 联合国对伊朗核计划的监督若无法延续，可能削弱国际社会对伊朗核活动的透明度，增加地区紧张局势和核扩散风险。

entities.explain: 美国主流大报，以国际新闻报道和调查性报道著称，在国际舆论中有较大影响力

cards.summary: 联合国调查人员发布报告称，美国对伊朗一所学校的空袭导致一百多名儿童死亡，相关失误"超出了疏忽范畴"，可能构成战争罪。报告还提到同一天另一起空袭造成约22名平民死亡。调查人员认为这些事件并非简单的操作失误，而是涉及更严重的责任问题。
cards.relevant: 该报告将美国军事行动定性为可能构成战争罪，涉及国际人道法的核心问题，可能影响美国与伊朗关系及国际社会对美军海外行动的审视。
cards.context: 美国此前对伊朗境内目标发动军事打击，其中一次空袭击中了一所学校，造成大量儿童死亡。联合国对此展开调查，旨在评估该袭击是否违反国际人道法。
cards.source_analysis: 纽约时报是美国的自由派主流媒体，在国际事务报道中常持批评性视角，尤其对美国政府军事行动的合法性审查较为严格。
cards.social_impact: 空袭造成一百多名儿童死亡，另一起空袭致22名平民死亡，事件涉及大量平民伤亡，可能引发国际社会对美国军事行动的广泛谴责和追责呼声。

cards.summary: 联合国专家表示，有合理理由相信美国今年2月对伊朗米纳布一所小学和拉梅尔德一个体育综合设施实施的致命空袭构成战争罪。美国方面尚未承认发动了这些袭击。联合国专家的结论虽无法律约束力，但具有重要的国际道义和政治影响力。
cards.relevant: 若联合国专家结论被进一步采纳，可能推动国际刑事追责程序，并加剧美国与伊朗之间的紧张关系，同时引发国际社会对军事打击中平民保护问题的关注。
cards.context: 2025年2月，伊朗米纳布一所小学和拉梅尔德一个体育综合设施遭到致命空袭，造成人员伤亡。美国未承认实施这些打击。联合国专家对此展开调查后得出上述结论。

For their latest report to the UN Human Rights Council, the mission's three independent experts investigated two of the deadliest attacks on civilians during the conflict. On 28 February, when the US and Israel launched their war against Iran, Tomahawk missiles struck Shajareh Tayyebeh Primary School in the southern town of Minab, killing at least 156 people, including 120 children, according to local authorities. cards.social_impact: 伊朗代表团入境涉及美国签证政策与联合国东道国义务的长期争议，也牵动中东局势走向，影响范围覆盖美伊双边关系及地区安全。

cards.source_text: Wife of US scholar jailed in China asks Trump to raise arrest at Xi meeting - Published The wife of a US scholar imprisoned in China on charges of spying and endangering national security has asked President Donald Trump to secure his release when he meets Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House next week. U Min Zin, the director at a think tank focused on Myanmar, was arrested on 3 June after travelling to the Chinese city of Kunming for an academic conference. "I'm deeply hopeful that President Trump will raise my husband's case with President Xi Jinping at the summit next week," his wife, Sylvia Zin, testified to Congress on Wednesday. Xi is due to arrive for a state visit to Washington DC on Wednesday. It comes after Xi hosted Trump for a visit to Beijing in May. Ahead of the meeting, families of prisoners being held in China have travelled to the US capital to advocate for their release. As the US marks the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks launched by al-Qaida against targets in Washington and New York, the statistics underline the continued expansion of the veteran organisation in parts of Africa – in stark contrast with its relative weakness elsewhere. Compiled by Acled, which stands for Armed Conflict Location and Event Data, the statistics focus on the centre of Islamic militancy in three countries – Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger – which together comprise a huge and hotly contested zone at the heart of the strategic Sahel region. According to the respected non-profit organisation, incidents of violence with jihadist groups present in the three countries have soared from 63 in 2016 to 2,845 in 2025. So far this year, 2,145 events have already been logged. If current trends continue in coming months, an annual total of well over 3,000 events appears likely. Though total deaths from terrorism globally have fallen to their lowest level since 2008, those in the Sahel have risen sharply. “Terrorism has become more geographically concentrated: the Sahel continued to record some of the world’s highest terrorism death tolls, with the UN recording more than 9,000 deaths from security incidents across Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger in 2025,” the 2026 report of the Global Peace Index noted earlier this year. In April, a joint offensive in Mali launched by the al-Qaida-linked group Jama’at Nusrat ul-Islam wa al-Muslimin (JNIM) and the Tuareg-dominated rebel group Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) targeted strategic towns, government forces and their Russian auxiliaries with ambushes, car bombs, drones and raids, inflicting significant casualties. When Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo did not return after going for a run on 9 September, her eight-year-old daughter alerted relatives, who contacted police. The 38-year-old’s body was found on Saturday and identified by relatives on Monday. The news of her disappearance had gone viral. cards.source_text: French police officer arrested over suspected far-right terror plot A French police officer who allegedly adheres to a 'violent radical far-right ideology' has been arrested on suspicion of plotting attacks against state interests and manufacturing 3D-printed weapons, sources told AFP Thursday. A policeman who follows "a violent radical far-right ideology" has been arrested in France on suspicion of plotting a terrorist attack, sources told AFP late on Thursday. Confirming a report by the TF1/LCI broadcaster, a judicial source said that the man was also suspected of having manufactured weapons, among other crimes. A separate source close to the case told AFP that the police officer, aged 35, was "apprehended on the street" on August 23. He has since been placed in detention while awaiting trial. According to TF1/LCI, the officer "is suspected of having planned to carry out violent attacks against the interests of the state" and of having "manufactured 3D-printed weapons", among other things. The policeman faces charges including preparing a terrorist act, the unauthorised manufacture or trade in weapons in connection with a terrorist organisation and unauthorised weapon possession. He is also charged with incitement to terrorism through social media. The police officer's lawyers had not responded to AFP as of Thursday evening. The news comes in the wake of revelations that France's far-right National Rally (RN) party expelled another policeman after body cam footage of him making racist comments sparked outrage. The RN's Marine Le Pen hopes to become France's president in next year's elections after years of seeking to make the anti-immigration party she inherited from her father more palatable to the wider public. (FRANCE 24 with AFP)

A cherished 16th-century Mexican manuscript that tells the history of the Aztecs in pictograms went on display Thursday in Mexico City, nearly two centuries after it was whisked off to France. The Codex Azcatitlan recounts the history of the Aztec civilization, from the creation of the Aztec Empire to its fall during the Spanish conquest, which ushered in Christianity. Mexico has been demanding for years that France return it but so far France has refused. Members of an Indigenous group that has campaigned for its restitution reacted ecstatically to seeing two folios from the precious document on display inside a glass case at the National Museum of Anthropology. "They hid our history from us, they stole it!" Emilia Mendoza of the Hnahnu community told AFP at the opening of the exhibition. "This is a battle won, a first step toward the restitution of these books that reside in other countries," she said. Speaking at the inauguration, Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco said the exhibition was about "reuniting a population with its (collective) memory." The pictograms "represent our history, the written voice of our ancestors, and the deep root of our identity," he said. 'Why isn't it in Mexico?' Written shortly after the arrival of the Spanish in the 16th century, the codex, or manuscript, is considered one of the most important accounts of Aztec culture. It narrates the migration from Aztlan, the mythical birthplace of Aztec civilization, to the promised land of Tenochtitlan, the forerunner of Mexico City. Scenes rendered in vibrant reds, blues, greens and yellows depict warriors in feathered headdresses and ritual acts in pyramid temples. France's National Library, which has maintained possession of it for over a century, loaned it to Mexico to commemorate 200 years of relations between the two countries. But Mexico, which has launched a push to recover colonial-era cultural objects held outside the country, wants France to go further and hand it back. cards.source_text: It sounds like a Disney movie: three wild dogs, all brothers, on an epic journey to find a home of their own after their family tells them to leave. They dodge cars and hunters in search of a new life, navigating bushmeat snares and the hostility of a human-dominated landscape until they find a new haven on the African savannah. But this is exactly what happened in Zambia last year, when three endangered African wild dogs made the longest-ever recorded single journey of any mammal from the continent. The brothers travelled more than 2,500 miles (4,100km) over eight months in their “dispersal” – when a young dog comes of age and must establish new territory to find a mate and start a family of their own. From point to point, starting in Kafue national park in western Zambia to their final destination in the Luangwa valley in the east of the country, the brothers covered 340 miles (546km), which is also a record. The epic single journey is almost equivalent to travelling the length of Chile by foot and farther than the famous wildebeest and zebra migration across the Serengeti in east Africa. The previous record was 2,418 miles, also made by African wild dogs, which moved between Loliondo, in northern Tanzania’s Ngorongoro district, and Tsavo West national park in southern Kenya in 2012. Dr Matt Becker, chief executive of the Zambian Carnivore Programme (ZCP), whose scientists were monitoring the wild dogs and have published their findings in the journal Ecology, says: “These extraordinary journeys show that natural connections between Africa’s wildlife strongholds still exist. But they also reveal how difficult and dangerous those journeys have become. “Rather than relying solely on fenced protected areas, these findings reinforce the value of investing in connected landscapes. The brothers travelled more than 2,500 miles (4,100km) over eight months in their “dispersal” – when a young dog comes of age and must establish new territory to find a mate and start a family of their own. items.title: ‘We are prey’: discovery of seven women’s bodies fuels anger over femicide in South Africa
items.summary: String of female murder victims found near Johannesburg’s international airport, including five in the past week The discovery of the bodies of eight women around Johannesburg’s international airport, including five in the past week, has prompted an outpouring of fear, grief and anger over a lack of progress in tackling femicide. When Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo did not return after going for a run on 9 September, her eight-year-old daughter alerted relatives, who contacted police. The 38-year-old’s body was found on Saturday and identified by relatives on Monday. The news of her disappearance had gone viral. Continue reading...

items.title: US to bar some South Africans over claims of anti-white discrimination
items.summary: Announcement of visa restrictions follows Trump’s false claims of ‘white genocide’ taking place in South Africa The US has announced visa restrictions on some South Africans as Donald Trump’s administration continues to claim that South Africa’s government racially discriminates against white minority Afrikaners. The announcement did not specify individuals who were barred from the US. Trump has spent his second term falsely claiming there is a “white genocide” in South Africa and railing against its affirmative action policies. Continue reading...

items.title: Al-Qaida and IS-linked violence in Africa’s Sahel belt set to hit record levels this year
items.summary: Twenty-five years after 9/11, figures compiled by conflict monitor underline how Sahel region has become centre of Islamist terror Islamist extremist violence in Africa’s Sahel region is set to reach historic highs after a series of sweeping offensives by groups linked to al-Qaida and Islamic State, according to new figures compiled by the conflict monitor Acled . As the US marks the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks launched by al-Qaida against targets in Washington and New York, the statistics underline the continued expansion of the veteran organisation in parts of Africa – in stark contrast with its relative weakness elsewhere. items.title: Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds
items.summary: Dozens of Bank of England directors and founding subscribers invested in trafficking of enslaved Africans The Bank of England and the British financial system were for centuries deeply involved in the enslavement and transatlantic trafficking of millions of African people, according to new research on Britain’s slavery history. Research by historians compiling the Register of British Slave Traders has found that the scale of the financial system’s involvement in enslavement is greater than previously known or acknowledged. The Bank of England, the central bank owned by the government since nationalisation by Clement Attlee’s Labour administration in 1946, had dozens of financiers involved in its foundation who were also significant investors in the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans.
